name: Scarab Wall
summary: At Silithus's southern edge, the Scarab Wall bars the way to Ahn'Qiraj. Stone and bronze dragonflight sorcery keep the ancient swarms sealed beyond it, as they have since the War of the Shifting Sands.

sections.title: Shield Against the Shadow
sections.body:
The Scarab Wall runs across the desert from east to west. It was raised a thousand years ago, after the War of the Shifting Sands. The qiraji nearly destroyed the night elf armies and their dragon allies before they drove the swarms back into their ancient kingdom.

To hold the qiraji there, the allies raised a great rampart of desert stone. The bronze dragonflight crowned it with a magical barrier. The wall cut the insectoid armies off from Kalimdor, yet their dread presence still hangs behind its stones.

sections.title: A Sealed Ruin
sections.body: Beyond the sandstone wall and its draconic wards lies Ahn'Qiraj, stronghold of the ancient qiraji. The wall was raised to imprison their armies after the War of the Shifting Sands. Its gates can be opened by ringing the Scarab Gong with the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, a relic tied to the dragons and Fandral Staghelm.

aliases: what is this wall in silithus
faq.answer: Stone and magic bar the southern edge of Silithus at the Scarab Wall. Beyond it lie Ahn'Qiraj and its ancient insectoid swarms, sealed in the desert ruins.

The night elves and bronze dragonflight raised the Scarab Wall together at the end of the War of the Shifting Sands. Stone sealed the qiraji inside, and the dragons wove a vast magical barrier above it.

faq.q: Why was the Scarab Wall raised?
aliases: why was the scarab wall built
faq.answer: The night elves and their dragon allies raised the Scarab Wall after driving the qiraji swarms back into Ahn'Qiraj. There they sealed them away, bringing the War of the Shifting Sands to an end.

faq.q: Can players go past the wall?
aliases: can you go past scarab wall
how to get past wall in silithus
faq.answer: The Scarab Wall seals Ahn'Qiraj, but its gates can be opened by ringing the Scarab Gong with the Scepter of the Shifting Sands.

angles.text: For night elves, the Scarab Wall recalls the terrible sacrifices of the War of the Shifting Sands, when an entire generation was lost to halt the swarm.
As a druid, you feel life unnaturally suppressed around the wall. Ancient wards struggle to contain a corruptive blight beneath the earth.
